newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks finish higher on U.S. market boost. [CORRECTED 17:37 GMT]
newsitem.headline: French stocks finish higher on U.S. market boost. [CORRECTED 17:37 GMT]

text.p: French shares finished higher on Thursday, lifted in the afternoon by strength in U.S. stock and debt markets after opening lower and spending most of the session stuck nearly unchanged.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closer 17.46 points or 0.75 higher percent at 2,349.08 while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 8.5 points at 1606 GMT.
Volume was a hefty 8.1 billion francs.
U.S. markets climbed on news that December producer prices rose 0.1 percent excluding food and energy. For 1996, overall producer prices rose 2.8 percent, the smallest gain since 1993.
* Paribas up 4.02 percent at 354.20 (corrects from 345.20) francs after announcing that its Credit du Nord unit would be sold to Societe Generale.
* Societe Generale ended 2.22 percent higher at 552 francs. It was the second most heavily traded share on the bourse.
Traders said the deal keeps merger interest alive. Rumours had been circulating recently over an acquisition in the financial sector although the names were vague.
*Saint Gobain closed 4.85 percent higher at 779 francs after buy reccommendations from at least two French brokers as interest in cyclical stocks is perking up.
Broker Leven says St Gobain is undervalued by as much as 30 percent in relation to the Paris Bourse's price/earnings ratio.
* Valeo ended up 0.96 percent at 348.30 francs after posting 1996 sales up 14.4 percent, in line with expectations.
* Rhone-Poulenc closed down 0.18 percent at 165.90 francs despite denial by state-owned CDR that it was planning to sell its holding in Rhone.
* Alcatel Alsthom closed up 0.82 percent at 431 francs as investors bet on benefit from buying Thomson-CSF, contrary to earlier fears a buy would be a burden.
The government says it is still studying privatisation options for Thomson-CSF and has not decided between a public offer or private tender.

* Accor closes 0.31 percent higher at 655 francs after revealing it is in talks to form a joint venture with Spanish hotel chain NH, which is 64 percent controlled by Cofir. Cofir shares were up 5.33 percent.
* Moulinex closed up 5.69 percent at 130 francs as share continues to benefit from expectations restructuring plans will help company. Traders consider the stock a long-term play.
* Generale des Eaux closed up 3.06 percent at 708 francs as stock keeps climbing after announcement of success in cutting debt and reaffirming its profit forecast for the year.
